Drill cores at Jaguar Uranium's Berlin project in Colombia. Credit: Jaguar Uranium
Posted By: Blair McBride November 25, 2026
An initial resource from Jaguar Uranium (NYSE-A: JAGU) for its Berlin critical metals project in Colombia outlines 40% more inferred tonnes but about half the uranium grade and 29% fewer contained pounds than a historical estimate by the previous owner.
Berlin holds 937,000 indicated tonnes grading 561 parts per million (ppm) uranium oxide (U 3 O 8 ) for 1.2 million lb. U 3 O 8 and 11.3 million inferred tonnes at 562 ppm U 3 O 8 for 14.1 million lb. U 3 O 8 , Jaguar reported Wednesday . SLR International prepared the resource, effective Nov. 5.
Berlin held 600,000 indicated tonnes grading 0.11% U 3 O 8 for 1.5 million lb. and 8.1 million inferred tonnes at 0.11% U 3 O 8 , or 1,100 ppm, for 19.9 million lb., as reported by former owner U3O8 Corp. in 2012 . The earlier estimate used a uranium-grade cutoff of 0.04%, while Jaguar’s uses $245 (C$350) per tonne as its net smelter return cutoff, incorporating the value of other metals, and limits the resource to material considered potentially mineable underground.
“We have defined a uranium resource alongside a suite of critical mineral and strategic metal co-products, including rare earth oxides, vanadium, nickel, zinc, molybdenum and phosphate,” Jaguar CEO Steven Gold said in a release, noting that the metals occur across 2.9 km of a 10.5-km trend that’s open to the north.
“With a strong balance sheet and no debt, we are well-funded to advance further exploration activity.”
Jaguar shares rose 4.7% to 63.4¢ apiece by 10:18 a.m. Wednesday in New York, for a market capitalization of $12.8 million.
Critical metals spread
Berlin’s other metals could be important to its economic prospects. Jaguar says material grading 400 to 600 ppm U 3 O 8 can qualify for the resource because the potential value of vanadium, phosphate, rare earths and other metals lifts it above the $245-per-tonne net smelter return cutoff.
Berlin is about 150 km northwest of Bogotá in Caldas department.
The 937,000 indicated tonnes also grade 50,474 ppm phosphorus pentoxide (P₂O₅) for about 47,300 contained tonnes. Other grades include 3,170 ppm vanadium pentoxide (V₂O₅) for 2,970 tonnes, zinc at 1,830 ppm for 1,715 tonnes and nickel at 1,094 ppm for 1,025 tonnes.
Jaguar plans additional drilling, including infill to upgrade inferred resources to indicated, though it hasn’t specified targets in metres.
The company acquired Berlin in 2024 from Green Shift Commodities (TSXV: GCOM), formerly U3O8 Corp., in a cash-and-shares deal that included C$20,000, 1.21 million Jaguar shares and a 1% net smelter return royalty at closing. Jaguar paid another C$1 million and issued shares valued at $15.3 million when it listed in February.
